name: Shock-Cohort Residual Reversal (SCRR): event-gated, hold-to-horizon, beta-hedged liquidity provision on the PIT daily OHLCV panel
mechanism:
DATA FLOW. Minute table -> `trader/data.py:aggregate_asset_daily` (true UTC-midnight OHLCV incl. volume and trade_count, `trader/data.py:~142-190`) -> a NEW (T,A,5) OHLCV panel reader (both existing readers return CLOSE only: `build_daily_panel_from_db` `:~192-227`, `read_ohlcv_daily` `:~268-317`; the `ohlcv_daily` DDL already carries open/high/low/volume `:~234-247`, so this is a ~40-line extension, the only code prerequisite) -> PIT universe via `build_pit_universe` (`:426`) + the 819 liquidity filter (`:57-92`) + `strategy.present_mask` (`trader/strategy.py:112-120`). Per date t over live assets: r_m,t = equal-weight market return; beta_i,t from a trailing 90-d causal regression, SHRUNK 50% toward 1 (cascade days blow up OLS beta); residual e_i,t = r_i,t - beta_i r_m,t; sigma_i,t = Garman-Klass (or Rogers-Satchell) range vol over 30 true daily bars, NOT Yang-Zhang: on a 24/7 venue open_t == close_{t-1} to within one minute so the overnight-gap term is identically ~0 and "overnight gap" is undefined as a feature. Shock statistics: z_e = e_i,t/sigma_i,t; RZ = log(H/L)_t / median_30 log(H/L); VZ = log(V_t / median_30 V); cross-sectional dispersion D_t = MAD_i(e_i,t), DZ = D_t / median_30 D. EVENT (asset level): |z_e| >= 2.5 AND (RZ >= 2 OR VZ >= 2). CASCADE-DAY flag: DZ >= 1.5 AND >= 8 assets trigger. Cohort C_t = the event set at t. Everything is causal at close t.

LEARNED OBJECT, TARGET, LOSS. Target y_{i,t,h} = (sum_{s=1..h} e_{i,t+s}) / sigma_i,t for h in {1,3,5} (h=3 primary), i.e. the forward MARKET-RESIDUAL return standardised by range vol - same target family as TASK_915 so results are directly comparable. Learned object f_theta: (z_e, RZ, VZ, DZ, 1{e<0}, dollar-volume rank, days-since-listing, h) -> E[y | event]. Primary model class: hierarchical Bayesian linear model on EVENT ROWS ONLY, y = -(k0 + k_R*RZ + k_V*VZ + k_D*DZ + k_S*1{e<0}) * z_e + a_i + eps, asset random effect a_i ~ N(0, tau^2) with tau^2 learned (partial pooling: most of the 273 assets have < 20 events), Huber loss (delta = 2 sd) with inverse-variance weights; secondary arm: LightGBM with monotone constraint (E[y] non-increasing in z_e), depth <= 3, <= 8 leaves, <= 200 trees, on the same ~5-10k event rows; multi-task across h (shared trees / shared slopes with per-h intercepts). Refit: expanding window, once per calendar year, purge >= h days, development span 2018-10 -> 2023-12, hold-out 2024-01 -> 2026-06 touched exactly once after the SPEC sha256 is committed. Per-cohort N is 8-60 so no per-cohort statistic is read; only pooled, DATE-CLUSTERED slopes and out-of-sample book PnL are read.

CONTROL LAW AND EXECUTION. At close t, for each i in C_t: predicted h-day residual edge m_i = f_theta(.)*sigma_i,t; cost c_i = 2*21 bp (entry+exit taker, `trader/backtest.py:188-190` charges |delta pos| at 21 bp/side) plus, for any SHORT leg, h * borrow (Kraken margin rollover 0.02-0.04%/4h on most crypto = 12-24 bp/day, BTC 0.01-0.02%/4h = 6-12 bp/day; fee schedule fetched 2026-09-05). ANALYTIC gate (not learned, pre-registered): trade iff m_i - sqrt(delta)*se(m_i) - c_i > 0 (the DRO/shrinkage form the loops panel kept). Size w_i = sign(m_i) * min(cap_pos, (m_i - c_i) / (lambda * h * sigma_i^2)) - a one-shot Markowitz/GP full-trade solution, because there is NO re-trim: enter at close t, exit at close t+h, hold shares in between. Arm A (primary): LONG the losers cohort only, beta-hedge the cohort with a BTC (fallback ETH) SHORT of weight -sum w_i beta_i (cheap borrow, guaranteed margin availability). Arm B: long losers / short winners within the cohort, beta-neutral, restricted to margin-enabled pairs. Caps: |w_i| <= 2.5%, cohort gross <= 25%, total open gross <= 100% (spot-margin sum|w| <= 1), hedge counted in gross. Default state is FLAT; the book holds positions only inside open cohorts. Turnover per cohort = 2*gross_cohort (+hedge); at K = 40 cohorts/yr and 0.2 gross that is ~16 turnover units/yr = 0.044/day vs the trend book's 0.155/day (`trader/config.py:89-105`, `POWERED_RESULT.md` turn column) - 3.5x fewer cost events, each attached to a forecast of several hundred bp rather than a sign flip. Grading: write the cohort positions into a (T,A) pos matrix and score with the UNMODIFIED `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` at H=1 (`trader/backtest.py:235-283`) at 21 and 30 bp/side, plus a pre-registered carry term for the short legs (the scorer has no borrow model); report hold-shares vs constant-dollar accounting side by side (the scorer's constant-weight convention leaves daily drift re-trims uncharged - tactics panel correction 3).
math:
NOTATION AND STATED INPUTS (A = assumption to be measured in step 0; R = record). R: cost 21 bp/side on turnover, round trip 42 bp per unit weight (`trader/backtest.py:188-190`, `POWERED_RESULT.md` discipline line). R: alt-short borrow 12-24 bp/day, BTC 6-12 bp/day (Kraken fee schedule, fetched). A: post-shock residual daily vol sigma ~5% (alts 5-7%/day, residual ~0.8x), so an event |z_e|>=2.5 is a |e| >= 12.5% day; A: 3-day position sd ~10% (vol stays elevated after a shock). A: within-cohort residual correlation rho ~0.25 on cascade days, cohort size n_e ~12.

PER-EVENT ECONOMICS. Let kappa_h = fraction of the shock-day residual that reverses over h days (the learned quantity). Expected reversal per position mu = kappa_3 * |e| = kappa_3 * 12.5%: kappa 0.05 -> 0.63%, 0.10 -> 1.25%, 0.20 -> 2.5%. Net per-position edge: long leg mu - 0.42%; alt-short leg mu - 0.42% - 3*(12..24 bp) = mu - 0.78..1.14%; BTC hedge leg cost 3*(6..12) = 18-36 bp on the hedge notional. Per-position Sharpe per event SR_pos = (mu - c)/10%: long leg kappa 0.05 -> +0.02, 0.10 -> +0.08, 0.20 -> +0.21; alt-short leg at kappa 0.10 -> +0.03, 0.20 -> +0.15 (borrow eats the short leg at moderate kappa - hence Arm A hedges with BTC instead of shorting winners). Cohort Sharpe per event: SR_e = SR_pos * sqrt(n_e/(1+(n_e-1)rho)) = SR_pos * sqrt(12/3.75) = 1.79*SR_pos -> kappa 0.10: SR_e ~ 0.10 (Arm A), kappa 0.20: SR_e ~ 0.32. In Grinold terms SR_e = IC_cohort * sqrt(N_eff,cohort) with N_eff,cohort ~ 3.2, so the CONDITIONAL within-cohort IC must be ~0.06 (kappa 0.10) to ~0.18 (kappa 0.20) - i.e. 3-8x the unconditional daily IC bar of 0.02-0.03 (memo Sec 1.3), on ~1% of asset-days. That is the exact form of the "IC concentrated in regime-days" hypothesis.

FROM PER-EVENT TO THE GOALPOST. A book flat except inside K independent cohorts/yr has annualised per-decision Sharpe SR_yr = SR_e * sqrt(K) (flat days add zero mean and zero variance, so the sqrt(365) daily annualisation collapses to sqrt(K); exact if cohort PnLs are independent, slightly optimistic with h=3 overlap). Required K = (bar/SR_e)^2: for +0.97, SR_e 0.10 -> K = 94 cohorts/yr (an event cohort every 3.9 days, ~1100 asset-events/yr - essentially the WHOLE event population with no gate, all at kappa 0.10); SR_e 0.32 -> K = 9.2/yr (a dozen cascade days suffice). For +0.56: SR_e 0.10 -> K = 31; SR_e 0.32 -> K = 3. Event supply (A): 250 live assets in 2024-26 (`POWERED_RESULT.md` coverage table: BULL24 239, CHOP25 267 mean live) x 365 x ~1-1.5% conjunction rate = 900-1400 asset-events/yr on ~60-120 distinct event-dates; development span 2019-2023 has fewer live assets (25 -> 209) so ~2500-4000 asset-events total for fitting. STATEMENT OF NEED: the mechanism clears +0.97 net@21 iff EITHER kappa_3 >= ~0.18-0.20 on >= ~10-15 cascade cohorts/yr, OR kappa_3 >= ~0.10 on essentially every event cohort (~90+/yr); it clears +0.56 at kappa_3 ~0.10 on ~30 cohorts/yr. Bremer-Sweeney's equity number (-10% day -> ~+1.8% over 2 days, kappa ~0.18, memory) is the reason the upper scenario is not fantasy; Kraken slippage on cascade days is the reason the cost side is optimistic.

COST AT THE MECHANISM TURNOVER. K=40 cohorts x gross 0.2 x 2 sides = 16 turnover units/yr -> 16 x 21 bp = 3.4%/yr fee drag (vs 0.155/day x 365 x 21 bp = 11.9%/yr on the trend book, GIVEN); hedge borrow ~0.2 x 3 d x 9 bp x 40 = 0.2%/yr; Arm B alt-short borrow ~0.1 x 3 x 18 bp x 40 = 2.2%/yr. On a book with ~10-15% annualised vol (flat most days) the fee drag alone is 0.2-0.3 Sharpe - the mechanism is NOT cost-dominated; it is kappa-dominated.

DETECTION POWER. SD of an estimated annual Sharpe over T years ~ sqrt((1+SR^2/2)/T) ~ 1/sqrt(T): 2.5-yr hold-out (2024-01 -> 2026-06) -> SD 0.63, 95% CI half-width +-1.24, so "CI lo > 0 on the hold-out" requires a realised SR > ~1.24 (this binds TASK_915 G-C equally); full 7.5-yr span -> SD 0.37, CI excludes 0 at SR > 0.72. In cohort units: t = SR_e*sqrt(n_cohorts) >= 1.96 needs n >= (1.96/SR_e)^2 = 384 cohorts at SR_e 0.10 (~4 yr at 94/yr, or the whole span at ~50/yr), 38 cohorts at SR_e 0.32. Conclusion: the decisive Sharpe CI must be full-span 2019-2026; 2024-26 is a sign/magnitude hold-out for the slope kappa (thousands of asset-events, date-clustered SE), not a stand-alone CI window. Slope power: with ~3000 dev asset-events, ~150 distinct dates, per-event y sd ~2 (in sigma units), a kappa of 0.10 on a mean |z_e| ~3 has t ~ 0.3/(2/sqrt(150)) ~ 1.8 if dates are fully dependent, ~8 if asset-events are independent - so the date-clustered t is the honest statistic and it is ~3-4 at kappa 0.10 in the realistic middle.

MULTIPLICITY. E[max SR_N | H0] = SD * [(1-gamma)Phi^-1(1-1/N) + gamma Phi^-1(1-1/(N e))], gamma = 0.5772 (Bailey-Borwein-Lopez de Prado-Zhu 2014). Sensitivity grid z* {2,2.5,3} x conjunction {range, volume, either, cascade-day} x h {1,3,5} = 36 cells: SR0(36) = 0.63 x 2.15 = 1.35 on the 2.5-yr hold-out (above the bar - the grid CANNOT be selected on the hold-out), 0.37 x 2.15 = 0.79 on the full span. Hence ONE pre-registered primary cell (z*=2.5, "either", h=3, hierarchical model, Arm A) and White's Reality Check (stationary bootstrap over dates, 500 draws) over the 36-cell grid for the rest.
profit_source: FORECAST - exactly one: the conditional FIRST MOMENT of the h-day (h=3 primary) market-residual return of an asset, conditional on a same-day liquidity shock (extreme residual move coinciding with an extreme range and/or volume, optionally on a high-dispersion "cascade" day). Economically this is the liquidity-provision premium (Nagel 2012): compensation for absorbing forced flow (liquidation cascades, margin unwinds, panic exits), which is time-varying and largest in turmoil. It is NOT a rebalancing premium (there is no rebalancing; positions are held to horizon), NOT a market risk premium (beta-hedged; Arm A's only market exposure is the hedge residual), and the sparse turnover is cost AVOIDANCE that makes the forecast harvestable, not a profit source in itself. The learned quantity is kappa_h(state) = the fraction of the shock-day residual that reverses, as a function of range/volume/dispersion state and shock sign; the second-moment quantities (range vol, dispersion) enter only as CONDITIONING variables for the first moment and as the standardiser, never as the profit source.
why_learning: The closed-form estimator is a single pooled slope kappa_h = -cov(y, z_e)/var(z_e) over event rows (or per-asset slopes, which are hopeless at <20 events/asset). Learning is justified by three things that estimator cannot use efficiently: (1) PARTIAL POOLING across 273 assets with wildly different event counts - the hierarchical random effect a_i ~ N(0, tau^2) with tau^2 estimated from data is the optimal shrinkage between "one kappa for all" and "one per asset"; a fixed pooled slope discards the per-asset heterogeneity Bianchi-Babiak-Dickerson report (liquidity-provision returns concentrated in smaller, less liquid pairs), and per-asset OLS drowns in noise. (2) SIGN-FLIPPING INTERACTIONS: the literature says the conditional mean after a volume shock depends on whether it co-occurs with a price shock (Gervais-Kaniel-Mingelgrin: volume shock alone -> continuation/premium; Avramov-Chordia-Goyal and Bianchi et al: volume x lagged return -> reversal in illiquid names), and the reversal premium scales with the turmoil state (Nagel: VIX; here DZ). A pooled linear slope cannot represent kappa changing sign with the (price, volume) quadrant; the interaction terms or the monotone GBM can, and with only ~3000-10000 event rows a heavily regularised low-parameter learner (5-8 slopes + tau, or a depth-3 monotone GBM) is the right capacity - this is small-data learning, not deep learning. (3) MULTI-HORIZON SHARING: h=1,3,5 targets share the shock features; the multi-task fit borrows strength for the noisiest (h=5) target and yields the decay profile kappa_h needed to pick the hold horizon under cost. What learning does NOT buy here: it does not find the events (the event definition is analytic and pre-registered), it does not decide when to abstain (the gate is analytic), and it does not touch sizing beyond supplying m_i and se(m_i). If step 0 shows the interaction slopes are all within 1 SE of zero, the learned object collapses to the pooled slope and the row should say so.

bear_positive.argument: Market-neutral by construction (beta-hedged cohort in Arm A; beta-neutral long/short in Arm B), so the bear sign equals the sign of the conditional reversal premium, not of the market. Two forces make a positive 2022 read PLAUSIBLE: (i) liquidity-provision theory (Nagel 2012) and the equity evidence say the premium is LARGEST in turmoil, and 2022 is where the cascade-day count peaks (LUNA May, 3AC June, FTX Nov) - the event supply K is highest exactly in the bear; (ii) the record's only bear-positive behaviour is the trend book's short leg (BEAR22 +1.095 vs long-flat -2.471, LEDGER 898), i.e. bears are where cross-sectional dispersion is widest, which is this mechanism's raw material. What BREAKS it, in order of size: (1) delisting/insolvency losers - the 'buy the loser' left tail (LUNA, FTT, CEL-type paths to zero) is continuation, not reversal, and is concentrated in bears; only the 2.5% position cap bounds it (a -95% loser at cap costs 2.4% of book), the forecast cannot; (2) beta error on cascade days - OLS beta jumps when r_m = -15%, so the hedge is mis-sized and the 'residual' shock is partly beta error; shrunk beta and a hedged-vs-unhedged paired report are the mitigation, not a fix; (3) short-side costs and availability - alt rollover 12-24 bp/day (36-72 bp over h=3, more than the 42 bp fee round trip) plus the fact that only ~300 pairs are margin-enabled on Kraken (support page, fetched; long-tail alts are not) means Arm B's short-winner leg is both costlier and universe-restricted; Arm A avoids it by hedging with BTC/ETH (6-12 bp/day, always marginable) at the price of carrying idiosyncratic residual beta; (4) slippage on cascade days: spreads on alts are far wider than slip5 assumes; report at 30 and 40 bp/side. Net: BEAR22 positivity is a form check on the DEVELOPMENT span (2022 is in-sample for the slope fit), so it is a necessary-not-sufficient check; the unseen bear evidence is 2025-26 (CHOP25/2026H1), where cascade days were fewer and the read will be low-powered.

guards: 887 ADAPTIVE HOLD: flat is the DEFAULT state and the gate is ANALYTIC (m_i - sqrt(delta)se_i - c_i > 0 with pre-registered delta and c_i), not a learned abstention, so there is no fixed point to collapse to; the anti-HOLD check is a COUNT: pre-register the expected cohort rate from the development span (>= 20 cohorts/yr, >= 300 asset-positions/yr); FAIL if the hold-out realises < 50% of it or if > 30% of trigger-days gate every position to zero. The 887 attractor becomes a logged number, as the tactics panel demanded for its selector. 892 RE-TRIM DAMAGE: one entry, one exit at t+h, no intermediate re-optimisation, no daily renormalisation, hold-shares accounting; the only turnover is the pre-registered 2*gross per cohort; any variant that re-trims (e.g. GP partial trading toward a moving aim) runs as a separate arm and is compared PAIRED against hold-to-horizon; the scorer's constant-weight convention (uncharged drift re-trims, tactics-panel correction 3) is reported alongside hold-shares (830 SPEC:95-98 showed this moves BEAR22 gross by ~1 Sharpe). 813 SELECTION LUCK: (a) ONE primary cell frozen in the SPEC (sha256) before any hold-out read; (b) the DIRECTION (reversal) is pre-registered, with the continuation book as the paired control - a rule grid that is free to pick direction is what 813 ran; (c) cluster accounting by DATE: co-fired events on one day are one cluster (813's 142 fires were 6 episodes), all slope SEs date-clustered, minimum 40 distinct cascade-dates and 400 asset-events per cell in development before a cell may be read; (d) hold-out 2024-01->2026-06 touched once; (e) placebo family with the SAME per-asset event counts: circular-shift of each asset's event dates (dependence-preserving, zero fitting variance - the loops panel's null), plus a shock-day random-sign placebo; the realised book is reported as a percentile of 500 placebo draws; (f) White's Reality Check over the 36-cell grid (stationary bootstrap over dates) and SR0(N) printed beside every best cell: SR0(36) = 1.35 on the 2.5-yr hold-out, 0.79 on the full span, SR0(1) = 0 with CI +-1.24 / +-0.72. MULTIPLICITY SUMMARY: N = 1 for the verdict (primary cell), N = 36 for sensitivity with RC p <= 0.10 required; anything added after the SPEC is a new row. SURVIVORSHIP: PIT panel with dead coins retained (819 POWERED builder), so losers that went to zero are in the loser cohorts - the guard is the cap, and the report must show the loser-cohort PnL with and without the bottom-decile-by-subsequent-volume names as a DIAGNOSTIC only (never as a filter, since that is look-ahead). DATA QUALITY: volume on 2018-2020 and agg1m-sourced dead coins must pass a coverage check (share of zero/NaN volume days per asset-year) before VZ is trusted; assets failing it use the range-only conjunction.

why_not_falsified.argument: 813 is a different object on every axis: minute-scale 1-min bars on 64 train-window-locked SURVIVORS; single-asset DIRECTIONAL CONTINUATION triggers (Donchian/MA breakouts; B1 range expansion with dir = sign(close-open); B3 RV regime with dir = sign(mean return); C1 BTC lead-lag with dir = sign(ret_BTC)) - no trigger in the map bets on REVERSAL of a residual; test split 2024-11 -> 2025-04 only (5 months), n_events 6 and 28, then 0/48 on a 2023-24 hold-out; 42 bp charged per fire with no cross-sectional hedge, so BTC-driven co-firing was counted as many independent bets. SCRR is the opposite sign (reversal), cross-sectional and beta-hedged (co-firing is hedged, not multiplied), on the PIT 273-asset TRUE daily OHLCV panel over 2018-2026 with thousands of asset-events, with a shrinkage estimator instead of a threshold grid. What 813 DOES establish and SCRR inherits: the fire -> episode -> hold-out ladder and the n_events >= 20-30 floor, which SCRR raises to 40 dates / 400 asset-events per cell.

literature.ref: Nagel, S. (2012) 'Evaporating Liquidity', Review of Financial Studies 25(7) [NBER w17653 page fetched 2026-09-05]
literature.claim: Short-term reversal strategy returns are a proxy for the returns to liquidity provision; the expected return is strongly time-varying and predictable with VIX; Sharpe ratios rise substantially in turmoil (2007-09) and even industry-portfolio reversal earns high returns when VIX is high. Used here as the economic model: the shock-conditional reversal premium should scale with a turmoil-state variable (DZ, realised dispersion), which is why the conditioning variables enter the learned object.
literature.numbers: No magnitudes were quoted on the fetched page; the qualitative claims above are verbatim in substance. My recollection of the paper's reversal-strategy Sharpe rising several-fold in high-VIX months is NOT verified this session.

literature.ref: Bianchi, D., Babiak, M., Dickerson, A. (2022) 'Trading volume and liquidity provision in cryptocurrency markets', Journal of Banking & Finance [Semantic Scholar record fetched 2026-09-05; 55 citations]
literature.claim: Returns from liquidity provision via short-term reversal in crypto are 'primarily concentrated in trading pairs with lower levels of market activity'; 'expected returns from liquidity provision are amplified in smaller, more volatile, and less liquid cryptocurrency pairs'; the interaction between lagged returns and trading volume carries 'significant predictive information'. This is the direct crypto precedent for a volume x lagged-return conditional reversal and for the per-asset heterogeneity the hierarchical model shrinks. Its concentration in illiquid pairs is also the mechanism's main cost risk (slippage there is not 5 bp).
literature.numbers: Abstract quotes no magnitudes; horizon in the paper is weekly (recollection, unverified). Reversal size and cost survival not extracted this session.

literature.ref: Kitron, N. A. (2026) 'Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement' [Semantic Scholar record fetched 2026-09-05; venue unspecified, 0 citations]
literature.claim: At 15-minute horizons 90% of 183 Binance pairs show significant directional reversal, carried by signs not magnitudes; gross edge peaks at 1.3 bp per trade against a 5 bp round-trip cost - too small to clear spot costs. Independent confirmation of the repo's 897 result on the minute surface; irrelevant to daily cohorts except as a warning that reversal at short horizons is cost-bound.
literature.numbers: 90% of 183 pairs; 1.3 bp gross vs 5 bp cost.

literature.ref: Memon, H. (2026) 'Do Extreme Bitcoin Price Movements Persist or Reverse? Evidence from Daily Bitcoin Returns', International Journal For Multidisciplinary Research [Semantic Scholar record fetched 2026-09-05; low-tier venue, 0 citations, single asset]

Weak evidence, but the sign ASYMMETRY (losers reverse, winners continue) is exactly why Arm A longs losers and hedges with BTC rather than shorting winners.
literature.numbers: Thresholds 3/5/7%; horizons 1/3/5 d; sample 2014-09-17 to 2026-07-31; no magnitudes in the abstract.

literature.ref: Bremer, M., Sweeney, R. J. (1991) 'The Reversal of Large Stock-Price Decreases', Journal of Finance 46(2) [NOT fetched this session; from memory]
literature.claim: After one-day declines of >= 10% in large US stocks, prices rebound significantly over the following 1-2 days; the rebound is concentrated in the first two days. Used as the anchor for the kappa ~0.18 upper scenario and for h = 1-3 as the primary horizon.
literature.numbers: Recollection: mean rebound ~ +1.8% over two days after a -10% day (kappa ~0.18). Treat as unverified until the paper is read.

literature.ref: Da, Z., Liu, Q., Schaumburg, E. (2014) 'A Closer Look at the Short-Term Return Reversal', Management Science 60(3) [Semantic Scholar fetch returned 429; from memory]
literature.claim: Decomposes monthly reversal into a component driven by residual (liquidity-shock) returns, which reverses, and a component driven by cash-flow/industry news, which does not; reversal profits come from the residual component. Motivates the MARKET-RESIDUAL target and event definition here.

literature.ref: Avramov, D., Chordia, T., Goyal, A. (2006) 'Liquidity and Autocorrelations in Individual Stock Returns', Journal of Finance 61(5); Gervais, S., Kaniel, R., Mingelgrin, D. (2001) 'The High-Volume Return Premium', Journal of Finance 56(3) [both from memory]
literature.claim: ACG: short-horizon reversal is concentrated in high-turnover, illiquid stocks and is consistent with price pressure from non-informational trades. GKM: a volume shock WITHOUT a price shock predicts POSITIVE subsequent returns (visibility/continuation). Together they say the sign of the volume effect depends on the price-shock quadrant - the sign-flipping interaction that justifies a learned interaction model over a pooled slope.

literature.ref: Liu, Y., Tsyvinski, A., Wu, X. (2022) 'Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency', Journal of Finance 77(2) [from memory]
literature.claim: Cross-sectional crypto momentum at 1-4 week horizons is a priced factor. This is the OPPOSING force at h >= 5: unconditional weekly continuation would erode an event reversal held too long; it is why h=3 is primary and h=5 is a sensitivity cell, and why the kappa_h decay profile is part of the learned object.

literature.ref: White, H. (2000) 'A Reality Check for Data Snooping', Econometrica 68(5); Romano, J., Wolf, M. (2005) 'Stepwise Multiple Testing as Formalized Data Snooping', Econometrica 73(4); Bailey, D., Borwein, J., Lopez de Prado, M., Zhu, Q. (2014) 'Pseudo-Mathematics and Financial Charlatanism', Notices of the AMS [from memory]
literature.claim: White's RC gives the bootstrap p-value of the best cell against the benchmark over the full grid (stationary bootstrap over dates preserves the date clustering of cohorts); Romano-Wolf stepdown identifies which cells survive; BBLZ give E[max SR_N | H0] = SD*[(1-gamma)Phi^-1(1-1/N) + gamma*Phi^-1(1-1/(Ne))], gamma = 0.5772, used above to compute SR0(36) = 1.35 (2.5 yr) and 0.79 (7.5 yr).
literature.numbers: Formula as stated; numeric SR0 values are my arithmetic on it.

literature.ref: Kraken fee schedule, kraken.com/features/fee-schedule [fetched 2026-09-05, served in Czech]; Kraken support 'Margin trading pairs and their maximum leverage' [fetched 2026-09-05]
literature.claim: Margin opening AND rollover fees per 4 hours: most crypto pairs 0.02-0.04%, BTC 0.01-0.02%, USD 0.025-0.05% (= 12-24 bp/day alt shorts, 6-12 bp/day BTC, 15-30 bp/day USD borrow). Spot ladder (30-d volume): $0 0.40/0.80, $2.5k 0.30/0.60, $10k 0.22/0.38, $100k 0.12/0.25, $1M 0.06/0.18, $10M 0.00/0.10 maker/taker %. ~300 margin-enabled pairs (incl. commodities and tokenised stocks), 2-3x on most, 2-10x on BTC/ETH; eligibility restrictions apply. Consequences: no 16 bp tier exists (confirms the loops panel's point; note the tier BREAKS differ between the two fetches - $50k/$250k/$500k/$2.5M in the loops panel vs $2.5k/$10k/$100k/$1M/$10M here - so the operator's actual ladder must be written down); the short leg carries a borrow cost of the same order as the fee round trip over a 3-day hold, which the repo's scorer does not model.

controllability: High, and higher than anything the MuZero line produced. The deployable artifact is a bill of materials, not a checkpoint: (1) an event table per date (asset, z_e, RZ, VZ, DZ, sign) computed by ~30 lines of numpy from the OHLCV panel; (2) a fitted object with ~6-8 slopes plus tau^2 (or a depth-3 monotone GBM, dumpable as a rule list), refit once a year with a frozen recipe - no online adaptation, no self-play, no target that depends on the policy; (3) an analytic gate and sizing formula with three pre-registered constants (delta, lambda, caps); (4) a time-based exit. Every position is explainable in one sentence ('X fell 3.1 sigma on 4.2x median volume and 2.3x median range on a cascade day DZ = 2.1; predicted 3-day residual rebound 1.4% vs cost 0.42% -> long 2.1%, hedged with 1.5% BTC short'). Behaviour is bounded by construction: flat is the default; gross <= 100%, per-name <= 2.5%, per-cohort <= 25%; turnover = 2*gross per cohort, so the annual cost bill is known in advance from the cohort count; the 887 attractor is a logged count with a FAIL threshold; the 892 channel does not exist because nothing re-trims. Failure modes are visible in the logs the same day they occur (cohort count, gate rejection share, hedge ratio, hit rate), which is what 'better hold on policy' meant in the tactics panel. The mechanism is also cheap to KEEP honest: because it fires ~1-3 times a week, every live trade can be reconciled against its event row, and a live drift in kappa (hold-out slope shrinking) is detectable within a year at the date-clustered SE - unlike a daily policy whose OOS seed spread is 1.0-2.0 Sharpe (875). Weak points of controllability: the beta hedge is an estimate that is worst exactly on cascade days; and an operator override is needed for known insolvency events (exchange collapses, delistings) that OHLC cannot see - that override is a documented manual rule, not a learned one.
compute: CPU only; no GPU at any stage; the 64 GB cards are irrelevant to this mechanism. Panel: 273 assets x ~2800 days x 5 fields ~ 4M floats (~30 MB); feature build (betas, GK vol, medians, dispersion) is vectorised numpy, minutes. Event rows: ~5-10k over 2018-2026; hierarchical model = closed-form ridge with random effects / REML via statsmodels or a 200-line numpy EM, seconds; LightGBM on 10k rows x 8 features, seconds per refit x ~8 yearly refits. Scoring: reuse `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (2000-draw block bootstrap) - under a minute per cell; 36 sensitivity cells + 500 placebo draws + 500 Reality-Check bootstrap draws ~ 1-3 CPU-hours total. Whole kill experiment <= 1 CPU-day wall including reruns; RAM < 8 GB; safe_run-wrapped on gpu-server per the compute rules, workstation acceptable for the syntax/py_compile pass only. Human cost is the binding one: ~2-3 implementer-days (OHLCV panel reader ~40 lines; event/feature module ~200 lines; cohort-book -> pos-matrix writer with hold-shares accounting and a short-carry term ~150 lines; SPEC + placebo/RC harness ~200 lines), plus the TASK_899 backfill ingestion for 2026H1 volume/high/low, which is planner-owned and already staged.

kill_experiment.design: Two stages, both pre-registered in one SPEC (sha256 committed before any fit). STAGE 0 - MEASUREMENT, NO TRADING (the load-bearing half): on the PIT true-daily OHLCV panel 2018-10 -> 2023-12 (development span), under the frozen primary event definition (|z_e| >= 2.5 AND (RZ >= 2 OR VZ >= 2); cascade flag DZ >= 1.5 and >= 8 triggers), report per year: asset-event count, distinct event-dates, cascade-day count, volume-coverage share; then the pooled reversal slope kappa_h = -cov(y_h, z_e)/var(z_e) for h in {1,3,5} on EVENT rows with DATE-CLUSTERED SE, the same slope on NON-EVENT rows (the unconditional 1-5 d reversal = TASK_915's F1 feature), the loser-only and winner-only slopes, the interaction slopes (RZ, VZ, DZ, sign) from the hierarchical fit with tau^2, and the kappa_h decay profile. Plus the dependence-preserving null: circular-shift each asset's event dates (500 draws) and recompute kappa_3(event) to get the null distribution. STAGE 1 - THE BOOK (only if S0 passes): fit f_theta on 2019-2023 expanding (yearly refits, purge 5 d), walk-forward on 2019-2023 to fix lambda/delta/caps, FREEZE, then ONE run on 2024-01 -> 2026-06 (hold-out, first touch) and the full span 2019-01 -> 2026-06, Arm A primary, Arm B secondary, hold-to-horizon; scored by unmodified `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` at 21 and 30 bp/side plus a pre-registered short-carry term (12 bp/day alts, 6 bp/day BTC; upper bound 24/12 also printed), hold-shares AND constant-dollar accounting, hedged AND unhedged; the CONTINUATION book (same cohorts, opposite sign) as paired control; 500 event-date-shift placebos and the shock-day random-sign placebo; White's Reality Check (stationary bootstrap over dates, 500 draws) over the 36-cell sensitivity grid; SR0(N) printed for N = 1 and N = 36 on both windows; per-year and per-regime rows (BEAR22 form check in-sample; 2024, 2025, 2026H1 unseen); cohorts/yr and gate-rejection share (anti-HOLD count); loser-cohort PnL with/without the bottom-decile-by-subsequent-volume names as a DIAGNOSTIC of the delisting tail. Epoch and PIT frame pinned per LEDGER.md:28-41. Kill date 10 days from SPEC commit; anything added later is a new row.
kill_experiment.instrument: `trader/data.py` aggregation + PIT builder + 819 liquidity filter (existing) + a new (T,A,5) OHLCV reader; a new `experiments/9xx_shock_cohort/` module (event/feature build, hierarchical fit, cohort -> pos matrix writer, placebo/RC harness), <= 1 page SPEC; scorer = unmodified `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` (seed 819, n_boot 2000) at H=1 plus a declared carry term; statistics = date-clustered OLS/REML for slopes, block bootstrap for Sharpe CIs, circular-shift placebo, White RC. Same panel, target family and scorer as TASK_915 so the two rows are directly comparable and can share the data build.
kill_experiment.pass_fail: S0 PASS (gate to build anything): kappa_3(event) >= 0.08 with date-clustered t >= 3 on 2019-2023, AND kappa_3(event) - kappa_3(non-event) >= 0.04 with t >= 2 (the 'IC concentrated on shock days' test), AND the event kappa_3 exceeds the 95th percentile of the 500 date-shift placebos, AND >= 40 distinct event-dates and >= 400 asset-events. S0 FAIL -> the angle is dead as a separate mechanism: record the kappa table in the LEDGER as the measured conditional reversal on the daily PIT panel, hand the event indicators to TASK_915 as F3 features, build no book. STAGE 1 PASS (all of): (a) hold-out kappa_3 same sign, >= 50% of development magnitude, t >= 2; (b) primary-cell Arm A book net@21 on 2024-01 -> 2026-06 >= +0.56 with placebo percentile >= 95 and RC p <= 0.10, and positive in each of 2024, 2025, 2026H1; (c) full-span 2019-2026 net@21 >= +0.97 with block-bootstrap CI lo > 0 (the only window where the CI can exclude 0 at the bar) and net@30 >= +0.56; (d) BEAR22 positive (form check) and beats the continuation control by >= 1.0 Sharpe on both windows; (e) >= 20 cohorts/yr realised in the hold-out and <= 30% of trigger-days gated to zero; (f) hold-shares and constant-dollar accountings within 0.2 Sharpe of each other on the full span, or the difference is named. MARGINAL: (a)+(b) pass with (c) failing only on the CI -> record and hand to the gate ladder as a candidate needing live paper time, not a ship. Anything else -> FAIL; event-conditional daily reversal is closed on evidence, the kappa table stays in the LEDGER.
kill_experiment.cost: <= 1 CPU-day compute (no GPU); ~2-3 implementer-days plus one judge pass; requires the TASK_899 daily backfill ingested for 2026H1 high/low/volume; kill date 10 days from SPEC commit. Stage 0 alone is ~2 hours of CPU and could be run inside TASK_915's data build.

honest_odds: P(Stage 0 passes - a conditional 3-day residual reversal on shock days with kappa_3 >= 0.08, date-clustered t >= 3, clearly above the unconditional reversal, on 2019-2023) ~ 40-50%: the equity evidence for extreme-loser reversal is old and robust, the crypto liquidity-provision evidence (Bianchi et al.) points the same way, and 2021-2022 supply cascade days generously; against it, crypto weekly momentum and the fact that many crypto 'shocks' are news (listings, hacks, unlocks) with continuation. P(Stage 1 book clears +0.56 net@21 on the 2024-26 hold-out with placebo p <= 0.05) ~ 12-18%: kappa must hold out of sample in a period with fewer cascade days, and cascade-day slippage will be worse than slip5. P(full goalposts: +0.97 full-span with CI > 0, BEAR22 positive, >= 20 cohorts/yr, net@30 >= +0.56) ~ 6-10%. Unconditional P(goalposts) ~ 7%, i.e. roughly double the tactics-panel families (1-5%), about half the memo's conditional-on-G-A number for TASK_915, and below TASK_915's unconditional 10-15% - because SCRR is a SPECIAL CASE of the F1 x F2 x F3 interaction TASK_915's GBM cell could in principle find, and its independent value is (i) the power of an event-conditional estimator when the signal lives on 1% of asset-days (thousands of informative rows instead of 550k rows with 1% carrying signal) and (ii) a sparse hold-to-horizon control law that a quadratic-cost GP book handles badly for lumpy signals. Odds are deliberately not inflated by the 'few hundred bp per event' framing: the arithmetic shows the bar needs kappa ~0.18-0.20 on 10-15 cohorts/yr or kappa ~0.10 on ~90/yr, and the hold-out cannot by itself produce a CI that excludes 0 below SR ~1.24. The right sequencing is Stage 0 inside TASK_915's data build (two hours), the book only on S0 PASS; the row's chief value is that its FAIL is informative for TASK_915 too (it says the conditional-IC-on-regime-days escape hatch is shut).
open_doubts: Slippage on cascade days: slip5 is a calm-market number; alt spreads and depth on a -15% market day are far worse, and the mechanism trades ONLY on such days. Net@30 and net@40 must be shown; a 907-style markout on shock days (not calm days) is the honest calibration and does not exist.

Beta on cascade days: OLS beta from 90 calm days mis-sizes the hedge exactly when it matters; the 'residual' shock may be partly beta error, inflating the event count and the apparent reversal (a mean-reverting beta error looks like reversal). Shrunk beta, rank-residual events, and hedged-vs-unhedged paired reads are mitigations; a rolling-beta arm is a sensitivity cell, not the primary.

Sign asymmetry: positive shocks (listings, pumps) may continue; Arm B's short-winner leg may be negative gross AND pays 12-24 bp/day borrow, and long-tail alts are not margin-enabled. Arm A avoids it but carries idiosyncratic beta mismatch; neither is clean.
Weekly crypto momentum (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu) opposes reversal at h >= 5; the horizon race is empirical and kappa_h could turn positive by h = 5, which would also make h = 3 exits marginal.

Insolvency/delisting losers (LUNA, FTT, CEL): the left tail of 'buy the loser' is not forecastable from OHLC and is concentrated in bears; caps bound it to ~2.4% of book per name but a 2022-type cluster of 5-10 such names in one year is a -10 to -20% drawdown the Sharpe will show.

Hold-out power: 2024-26 has fewer cascade days than 2021-22; a true kappa of 0.10 may read as insignificant on the hold-out, and the full-span CI is dominated by 2021-22 where the slope was also fitted - the two-window pass criteria partially conflate estimation and confirmation.

Volume data quality: Kraken volume for 2018-2020 and agg1m-sourced dead coins may have zero/NaN days that fake VZ shocks; the coverage check is pre-registered but may remove exactly the illiquid names where Bianchi et al. say the premium lives.

UTC-midnight event clock: cascades straddle midnight; a rolling 24-h trigger with entry at the next minute is a different (and probably better) instrument that the daily engine cannot score; the daily version may under-read the effect.

Borrow cost is unmodelled in `trader/backtest.py`; the carry term added here is a declared constant from a fee page fetched once, not an observed number; the operator's actual margin and spot tiers remain unrecorded (loops panel point 1).

Overlap: with h = 3 and cohorts on consecutive days, cohort PnLs are not independent and the SR_e*sqrt(K) scaling is optimistic by the overlap factor; the gross cap and the block bootstrap handle it in the scorer but not in the design arithmetic above.

Literature depth: Nagel, Bianchi et al., Kitron and Memon were read at abstract level this session; Bremer-Sweeney, Da-Liu-Schaumburg, Avramov-Chordia-Goyal, Gervais et al., Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu and the multiplicity papers are cited from memory (WebSearch budget exhausted, Semantic Scholar rate-limited) - the kappa ~0.18 anchor in particular must be verified before it is used in a SPEC.

Relation to TASK_915: if TASK_915's F1 reversal cell already reads a significant unconditional 1-3 d residual reversal, the event conditioning may add little; if it reads zero, Stage 0's kappa(event) - kappa(non-event) contrast is the whole question. The two rows should share one data build and one SPEC appendix rather than run as separate lanes.
